title: Quantity of Heat — MCQs
description: Newton's law of cooling, water equivalent, latent heat and change of phase.

questions.q: Newton's law of cooling is valid when:
options: The temperature difference is more than 30 °C
The temperature difference is small (about 20 °C or less)
Convection is the main mode of heat loss
questions.explanation: The law holds only for small temperature differences between the body and its surroundings, when the rate of heat loss is proportional to the temperature difference.

questions.q: In the method of mixture, the heat capacity of the calorimeter is usually expressed as its:
questions.explanation: The water equivalent W = m_cal c_cal / c_w is the mass of water that absorbs the same heat as the calorimeter for the same temperature rise.

questions.q: While ice is melting at 0 °C, the heat supplied is used to:
options: Increase the kinetic energy of the molecules
questions.explanation: During a change of phase the temperature (and hence the average kinetic energy) stays constant; the latent heat increases the potential energy by working against intermolecular forces.

questions.q: The SI unit of specific latent heat is:
questions.explanation: Specific latent heat is heat per unit mass, L = Q/m, so its unit is J kg⁻¹. There is no temperature term because the temperature does not change.

questions.q: When steam condenses to water at 100 °C, it:
questions.explanation: Condensation is the reverse of vaporization, so the latent heat of vaporization is released. This is why a steam burn is more severe than a burn from water at 100 °C.
